feedback: Strong, well-layered implementation; all hard gates green and AC-001..009 satisfied. To raise the score, address risk_control and minor maintainability gaps: (1) Wire rate control into production: route.ts:135-139 calls runItems without delayMs, so bulk commit hits Rakuten/Yahoo APIs with zero inter-item delay despite the task's '過負荷をかけない' requirement. runItems already supports delayMs+sleep (result.ts:53-69, tested in result-summary.test.ts) — pass a sensible delayMs (and optionally make it body-configurable) for the commit path. (2) Remove dead/ambiguous status: ItemStatus 'skipped' (types.ts:15) is never produced by executor/route, so summary.skipped is always 0 — either populate it (e.g. for invalid/empty cases) or drop it to avoid misleading UI. (3) Step precision: a multi-SKU item with a resolved category reports step 'register' (executor.ts:145) which is misleading; consider a dedicated step/marker for SKU/advanced skips (the error text does explain the reason, so low priority). (4) Optional: extract the shared findExistingProduct into a reusable lib to avoid the duplication between import route and migrate route (kept duplicated here deliberately to preserve AC-006; acceptable but note it). (5) Optional robustness: large lists run in one synchronous HTTP request and could hit serverless/timeout limits — document a recommended batch size or chunk the input.
risks: Production bulk commit applies no rate limiting (route omits delayMs); many items could overload Rakuten/Yahoo APIs even though runItems supports throttling.
Single synchronous HTTP request processes the whole list; large lists risk request/serverless timeouts with partial commit.
ItemStatus 'skipped' is declared but never emitted, so summary.skipped is permanently 0 (potential UI confusion / dead path).
hasAdvancedYahooSettings only checks yahoo_grouping_enabled; other advanced Yahoo settings (if any) would not be detected and could be auto-migrated.
findExistingProduct logic is duplicated between import route and migrate route; future schema/matching changes must be kept in sync in two places.
recommended_next_changes: Pass delayMs (and optional body override) to runItems in route.ts commit path to enforce inter-item throttling required by the task.
Either emit 'skipped' for an actual condition or remove it from ItemStatus/summary to keep the contract honest.
Add a route-level commit (dryRun:false) test asserting write deps are invoked and publish flag is threaded, complementing the executor unit tests.
Introduce a distinct step/marker for SKU/advanced-setting skips so per-item step is not mislabeled as 'register'.
Consider extracting shared findExistingProduct into a reusable helper to remove duplication while preserving existing-route behavior, and document recommended batch size for large lists.
